newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Le Pen would "allow migrants to leave".
newsitem.headline: France's Le Pen would "allow migrants to leave".

text.p: French far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen, comparing foreign immigrants to birds of the field, said on Friday his policy was not to expel them but "allow them to leave."
"When you have a cherry tree, you will see swarms of starlings arrive just when the cherries are ripe and you are about to pick it," Le Pen told Radio France Inter.
"You can make all the noise you want, they won't leave until all the cherries are gone," he said.

"I say we should stop giving foreigners what attracts them and explain to them we don't have the means to support them or even to give them employment. They'll leave by themselves," Le Pen said. "It's not a question of sending them back, we'll allow them to leave," he said.
Le Pen's stated policy so far has been that foreigners from third world countries should be expelled if they sought to stay in France longer than a year. Several million people would be affected.

He added that, if he were in power, France would cut aid to foreign heads of state, "since the money generally ends up in Swiss banks," and use the funds to help immigrants re-settle in their home countries.
Le Pen's National Front party is generally credited with around 15 percent of voter support for France's forthcoming May 25/June 1 general election.
